You develop our presence in Flanders among professional advisors: accounting firms (10+ people), notaries, family offices and independent wealth advisors. Your job is to understand how these firms work with their private clients, identify where wealth planning creates value for them, and show how we help them deliver it.

This is consultative selling. Sales cycles typically run from 5 to 9 months, and up to 18 months with larger organisations. Your credibility with partners and senior advisors rests first on your understanding of their profession and of private wealth matters. Sales technique comes second.

We're a technology provider. Your role is to understand advisors' needs and the wealth issues they handle, not to advise their end clients.
What you will do
Prospecting and discovery

• Work from an existing, qualified target list of firms and decision-makers in Flanders
• Lead in-depth discovery conversations with partners to understand their practice, their clients' wealth issues and their growth ambition.
• Translate these needs into concrete use cases for our company.
Advising and convincing

• Discuss succession, gifting and wealth structuring topics with advisors on an equal footing, and connect them to what the platform does
• Run tailored demos built around realistic client situations
• Answer business and technical questions, and bring in product or domain experts when needed
• Follow opportunities over long cycles, from first conversation to signature
Pipeline and network

• Manage your opportunities and forecasts in HubSpot
• Develop your network through professional associations, events, webinars and partnerships
Collaboration

• Work closely with our VP Sales and our Revenue Team Lead
• Share field insights with Marketing and Product: client needs, objections, gaps What we are looking for
Essential

• In-depth knowledge of Belgian private wealth: succession and gift planning (including Flemish rules), matrimonial regimes, life insurance, holding and company structures, real estate, and the related tax aspects
• Professional experience in a wealth-related environment: private banking, wealth planning or management, insurance brokerage, estate planning, tax advice, accounting or notarial practice
• The ability to hold credible, substantive conversations with partners and senior advisor.
• Fluent in Dutch and English (our working language)
A strong plus

• Familiarity with how accounting firms, notaries or independent advisors work: business models, client relationships, regulatory constraints, current challenges
• An existing network among Flemish advisors
• French
Personal qualities

• Curiosity and rigour: you like to understand before you propose
• Patience and consistency over long cycles, and relationships built to last
• Sound commercial instinct: you sense when to move forward, when to wait, and how to turn a good conversation into an opportunity
• Autonomy and an entrepreneurial mindset: you shape the role as the market develops
Formal sales experience is not a prerequisite. If you come from accounting, tax or wealth advisory and want to move into business development, we would like to hear from you.
 What we offer
• Real ownership in a market where our company already has references, active leads and a qualified target list
• Close support from experienced colleagues in sales and wealth planning
• Room to grow as our company expands into new markets
• Hybrid work, with regular field presence in Flanders
• Employee or freelance status, a package based on seniority, and commission on sales

Drive business growth by prospecting new B2B clients, developing long-term relationships and promoting innovative digital solutions across the Brussels region. Description

• Understanding customer challenges and presenting tailored digital solutions

A successful Field Sales Representative should have:

As Customer Service Specialist, you will be responsible for managing a portfolio of professional customers and ensuring a seamless customer experience throughout the entire order and service lifecycle.

Client Details

Our client is an international organization operating in a highly technical environment. The company collaborates with customers across multiple sectors and is known for delivering customized solutions and long-term service partnerships.

Description

Technology plays a key role in supporting business performance, operational continuity, and long-term growth.The organization combines the stability of an established international business with an evolving operating model and a strong focus on continuous improvement.To support this transformation, they are looking for their future Head of Network Infrastructure.The position offers an international working environment, exposure to strategic initiatives, and the opportunity to contribute to major technology decisions while collaborating with teams across multiple countries and functions.

Security & Risk Management

• Support compliance, risk mitigation, disaster recovery, and business continuity initiatives.
• Contribute to the protection of both corporate and operational environments.
Vendor & Stakeholder Management

• Oversee contract performance, service quality, and budget management.
• Work closely with business leaders, enterprise architects, and regional IT teams to prioritize initiatives and investments.
Leadership

• Lead and develop a global team of infrastructure and network professionals.
• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
• Drive capability development and succession planning within the organization.

The ideal candidate combines strong infrastructure and networking expertise with strategic leadership capabilities and experience operating in large international environments.Experience

• Proven experience managing enterprise infrastructure and network services.
• Strong background in multinational or highly distributed organizations.
• Experience leading geographically dispersed technical teams.
• Demonstrated success managing third-party providers and large-scale service delivery environments.
Technical Knowledge

• Knowledge of infrastructure governance, service management, and operational excellence frameworks.

Leadership & Soft Skills

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
• Ability to influence senior leadership and cross-functional teams.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
• Results-oriented mindset with a focus on service quality and continuous improvement.
• Comfortable navigating complex international environments and transformation programs.
Languages skills 

• English is mandatory, as it is the primary working language within the international organization and across global stakeholders.
• French or Dutch is strongly preferred, given the Brussels-based location of the role and the interactions with local and regional teams.

Most warehouse jobs are about keeping things running. This one is about keeping things running while you rebuild them.
 

My client, an international manufacturer, wants a Warehouse Manager who can run a large operation and has the appetite to change how it works. You get the mandate to shape the team, redesign the flows and bring LEAN into daily practice. You lead through your Team Leaders and sit on the operations management team.
 

What you are responsible forThe warehouse has two customers. One is the production floor, which needs materials on time and in full to keep the lines going. The other is the end customer, who expects a complete and correct delivery. You own both flows, from the moment goods arrive at the dock until they leave the site.
 

Running the operation
 
 

• You plan and steer receiving, storage, picking, packing and shipping. 

• When volumes peak or dip, you move people and capacity to where they are needed. 

• Every goods movement has to be in the ERP system correctly and on time. You make sure it is. 

• You decide how the space is used and change the layout when the flows change. 

• Forklifts, scanners and other equipment stay in good shape under your watch.  

Getting stock rightProduction and shipping only work when the numbers in the system match what is on the shelf. You take ownership of that. You set up structured cycle counts and follow up on every deviation. When something is off, you look for the cause in the process and fix it there. You keep master data, locations and labelling up to date, and you make sure every item can be traced.
 

Improving how the warehouse worksThis is where you leave your mark. You define the vision and standards for the warehouse and you apply LEAN tools such as 5S, kanban and just-in-time replenishment. You look at every flow with a critical eye and take out what adds no value, like waiting time, double handling and buffers nobody needs. Lead times from receipt to storage and from order to shipment go down. You anchor the improvements with standard work, visual management and clear procedures, and you keep the documentation and training material current.
 

Leading the team
 
 

• You lead, coach and develop your Team Leaders and, through them, the whole warehouse team. 

• You put people in the roles where they perform best and recruit when the team needs it. 

• You invest in training and cross-training, so the team can handle change. 

• You set clear targets and follow them up in a way people understand. 

• You hold performance and development conversations with your direct reports.  

SafetySafety comes first in your warehouse, for everyone. You make sure hazardous goods are stored correctly, loads are handled safely and the workplace stays clean and organized.
 

Budget and reportingYou report on the warehouse KPIs: accuracy, productivity, on-time delivery and safety. You prepare and manage the budget. When the warehouse needs new equipment, automation or a new layout, you build the business case.
 

Who you work withYou work closely with production, planning, quality, finance and IT. Externally you are the contact for carriers, suppliers and staffing agencies.

Background
 
 

• Bachelor’s degree in logistics, supply chain or industrial engineering, or equivalent experience. 

• At least 5 years, preferably more, as a warehouse or logistics manager in a production environment. 

• Experience leading a large team, preferably through team leaders. 

• You have improved inventory accuracy before and can show the results. 

• You have led LEAN or change projects on the floor.  

Knowledge
 
 

• You know warehouse processes inside out, from receipt to shipment. 

• You can design and improve material flows and layouts. 

• You use LEAN tools in practice. 

• Strong hands-on SAP experience (MM, WM or EWM). This is a must. 

• You are at ease with Excel and MS Office.  

Languages
 
 

• Fluent in Dutch, French and English.  

Who you areYou are on the floor as much as behind your desk. You analyze before you act, and once you decide, you follow through. Details matter to you because you know what a wrong count costs further down the line. You can explain why a change is needed and get your team behind it.

Your tasks:

As an Import & Export Coordinator at Lotus Bakeries, you play a key role in ensuring the seamless flow of goods across international markets. You coordinate import and export shipments, manage customs processes, and work closely with logistics partners, internal stakeholders, and customs authorities.
 

As part of the Import & Export team you will:
 
 

• Coordinate and manage international import and export shipments across multiple transport modes (ocean, road, air, and multimodal), ensuring timely delivery while optimizing logistics flows to balance service, cost, and operational requirements. 

• Prepare and submit import and export customs declarations in-house or in collaboration with customs brokers, ensuring accuracy and compliance with applicable regulations. Manage communication with local customs authorities and internal compliance teams to facilitate efficient customs clearance and the timely resolution of customs-related issues. 

• Monitor transport performance and proactively resolve issues such as delays, demurrage, detention, and other operational disruptions. 

• Maintain accurate shipping and customs documentation and follow up on discrepancies or corrective actions when needed. 

• Ensure accurate data entry and management across logistics and customs systems, including master data maintenance and customs decision tables in CAS, while safeguarding data quality, integrity, and compliance. 

• Act as the key operational contact for shipment-related questions and escalations and support the implementation of new logistics and customs processes. 
 

• You have a Bachelor or Master degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Transport, Customs, or a related field. 

• A (first) experience with international freight flows and customs formalities has given you a good understanding of ocean, road, and air transport. 

• With your strong organizational and communication skills in both Dutch & English, you are able to manage multiple priorities while maintaining an accurate and detail-oriented approach. 

• Working independently comes naturally to you, while you also enjoy collaborating with internal and external stakeholders to achieve shared goals. 

• A proactive, hands-on, and customer-focused mindset helps you adapt to changing priorities and remain effective under pressure. 

• You are comfortable working with Microsoft Office, and experience with SAP S/4 or customs systems is considered a plus. 

• Your genuine interest in international supply chain, trade, and customs motivates you to continuously learn and develop in this field.

jobs.occupation: Senior Process Engineer Wafer Bonding & Assembly
jobs.description:
What you will do
 
 

• You take ownership of temporary wafer bonding and debonding processes and tools, leading process qualification, continuous improvement, problem prevention and the introduction of new processes. Your scope includes:  

• Temporary wafer bonding and debonding  

• Wafer level packaging: (WLUF lamination, molding, CUF dispense, TCB D2W bonding)  

• You lead cross-functional improvements and structured problem-solving across research, engineering and operations, working with technical experts and equipment and material suppliers to resolve complex process and equipment issues.  

• You lead discussions between R&D and Engineering teams to ensure that experiments involving new materials and substrates follow agreed guidelines, including risk assessment.  

• You own process control and documentation for your tools, including recipe management, statistical process control (SPC), procedures, technical escalations, upgrades and recovery flows.  

• You coach process engineers, share technical knowledge and strengthen the engineering capability of the Wafer Bonding & Assembly team.  

• You will work in day-shift. 

Who you are
 
 

• You hold a Master’s degree in Science or Engineering, or have equivalent expertise gained through relevant experience.  

• You bring strong engineering judgement and an analytical approach, with demonstrated experience in process qualification, measurement, data interpretation and quality assurance.  

• You have at least 5 years of relevant experience in temporary wafer bonding and debonding and/or wafer level packaging including ownership of processes or tools and resolution of complex technical issues.  

• You work autonomously, prioritise technical challenges and deliver well-documented, lasting improvements with close attention to quality and detail.  

• You have demonstrated the ability to lead cross-disciplinary technical activities, align stakeholders and coach less experienced engineers.  

• You communicate fluently in English; additional languages are an asset.  

• You communicate technical findings, risks and recommendations clearly, and actively share knowledge to support colleagues and strengthen team expertise.

We are looking for an Audiovisual Event Logistics Technician to join our team in Brussels and provide hands-on logistical support for audiovisual and conference activities within an international institutional environment.

This role focuses on the preparation, transportation, installation support, and dismantling of audiovisual equipment used for conferences, meetings, and special events.

Your Role:

As an Audiovisual Event Logistics Technician, you will support the operational and logistical aspects of audiovisual events, working closely with AV technicians, coordinators, and event support teams.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Prepare, handle, transport, load, and unload audiovisual equipment and accessories.
• Assist with the installation and dismantling of temporary audiovisual and conference setups.
• Support technicians during event preparation, equipment installation, and removal.
• Prepare and organise cables, accessories, consumables, transport cases, and technical materials.
• Position equipment in meeting rooms, conference spaces, and event areas.
• Manage equipment storage, stock, inventory, and warehouse activities.
• Perform basic equipment inspections and report damaged, missing, or defective materials.
• Follow equipment lists, setup plans, packing instructions, and operational schedules.
• Ensure that equipment and working areas remain clean, safe, and properly organised.
• Support basic event equipment operations when required and under supervision. 
We are seeking a practical, organised, and reliable professional with experience in event logistics, audiovisual equipment handling, or technical event support.

The ideal candidate should demonstrate:

• Hands-on experience in event logistics, audiovisual equipment rental, or conference setup activities.
• Experience handling, transporting, installing, and dismantling technical equipment.
• Familiarity with temporary event setups, meeting rooms, or conference environments.
• Ability to follow operational instructions, equipment lists, and event schedules.
• Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
• Flexibility, teamwork, and the ability to work under time pressure.
• Good communication skills and a service-oriented attitude.
• Ability to perform physical tasks, including lifting equipment weighing at least 20 kg and climbing ladders with applicable safety rules and operational instructions.
Key Skills:

• Audiovisual Equipment: Basic knowledge of AV and conference systems used in meetings, events, and temporary installations.
• Event Logistics: Equipment preparation, transportation, loading, unloading, and dismantling.
• Warehouse & Inventory Management: Stock monitoring, storage organisation, equipment tracking, and inventory updates.
• Technical Support: Assistance with audiovisual installations and basic equipment operations under supervision.
• Digital Tools: Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook), Microsoft Teams, and inventory or planning tools.
• Safety Procedures: Understanding of safe equipment handling, lifting, transportation, and storage practices.
Desired Qualifications:

• Previous experience in audiovisual event logistics, equipment rental, event production, or technical logistics.
• Experience supporting AV technicians or event coordination teams.
• Familiarity with professional conference environments and audiovisual equipment.
• Experience working in international or multicultural environments.
• Languages: Fluent in either English or French, with a good working knowledge of the other language.
 
 
Joining CGIC means contributing to high-impact international projects in the IT and audiovisual sectors. You will work in a dynamic and multicultural environment, develop your expertise in professional audiovisual and conference technologies, and contribute to the smooth operation of critical meeting and conference services.
